nodes.name: Receive CSV
nodes.notes:
POST a CSV with header name,email,phone.
Accepts JSON {"csv": "..."} or form field csv=...

nodes.name: Parse CSV + Normalise
nodes.notes: Same normalisation rules as Task 1's normalize.py. Invalid identifiers become null, never guesses.

parameters.query:
WITH incoming AS (
  SELECT NULLIF($1, '-') AS email, NULLIF($2, '-') AS phone,
         NULLIF($3, '-') AS name, $4 AS row_number
),
candidates AS (
  SELECT pe.person_id, 'exact_email' AS method, 1.00 AS confidence,
         'incoming email equals stored email ' || pe.email AS evidence,
         0 AS priority
    FROM person_email pe JOIN incoming i ON pe.email = i.email
  UNION ALL
  SELECT pp.person_id, 'exact_phone', 1.00,
         'incoming phone equals stored phone ' || pp.phone_e164,
         1
    FROM person_phone pp JOIN incoming i ON pp.phone_e164 = i.phone
)
SELECT i.row_number::int          AS row_number,
       i.name                     AS incoming_name,
       i.email                    AS incoming_email,
       i.phone                    AS incoming_phone,
       best.person_id,
       p.full_name                AS matched_name,
       p.city                     AS matched_city,
       best.method,
       best.confidence,
       best.evidence,
       (SELECT count(DISTINCT person_id) FROM candidates) AS candidate_people
FROM incoming i
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT * FROM candidates ORDER BY priority LIMIT 1
) best ON true
LEFT JOIN person p ON p.id = best.person_id

nodes.name: Find Existing Person
nodes.notes: Read-only lookup. Priority: exact email, then exact phone - the same deterministic order as Task 1 matching. Parameterised ($1..$4), so no SQL injection. Always returns exactly one row per incoming row via LEFT JOIN LATERAL. Absent values travel as the sentinel '-' because n8n's query-replacement drops empty parameters, which would shift $4 away.
